overall: A person who knows the subject, telling you something they think you should know: clear, curious and warm, unhurried and a little dry. The read builds from a plain question through the mechanism, drops to its quietest at the stakes and the number, and lands lower and more certain than its middle.

lines.text: One scan in this long line can't wait. This is Houston Methodist, in the Texas Medical Center.
lines.intent: opens on the stakes, then places us
lines.note: Lands 'can't wait' plainly. Weight on 'Houston Methodist', an easy full stop before the place name.

lines.text: A radiologist reads them in order, top to bottom. So how does the urgent one get to the front?
lines.intent: poses the question the film answers
lines.note: Weight on 'urgent'. The question is genuine, not a hook, so it falls rather than lilts.

lines.text: It starts at the scanner. A router sends the right studies to the AI by itself, and technologists don't touch it. Before, that took setting up each scanner by hand.
lines.intent: shows where the work begins, the router
lines.note: Weight on 'scanner'. 'Before' lands dry, as a small aside about the old hand setup.

lines.text: Then an AI tool called Aidoc reads the images. It flags a possible problem and paints a heat map on the spot it means.
lines.intent: explains what the AI does, concretely
lines.note: Weight on 'heat map'. Even pace through 'flags a possible problem'.

lines.text: When the concern looks significant, that exam jumps to the top of the radiologist's worklist.
lines.intent: delivers the payoff of the mechanism
lines.note: Weight on 'top'. The one lift of the middle, then settle.

lines.text: Some scans can't wait. A pulmonary embolism is a blood clot that breaks loose and travels to the lungs. It can be deadly.
lines.intent: turns to why it matters, medical stakes
lines.note: Weight on 'embolism'. Drops on 'It can be deadly', said flat and still.

lines.text: With a stroke, one study estimates a typical patient loses 1.9 million neurons for every minute it goes untreated.
lines.note: Quietest line near the most important fact. The number lands flat, no lift on 'minute'.

lines.text: So Houston Methodist started with 18 super users testing it, then opened it to roughly 100 radiologists in June.
lines.note: Weight on 'roughly 100'. Plain tally, a little dry.

lines.text: Radiologists were skeptical at first. Ginny Torno, who leads the rollout, says even the most skeptical one called it a great tool.
lines.note: Weight on 'skeptical'. Name said evenly, slight smile in the closing phrase.

lines.text: She also says it isn't perfect, and Aidoc is upfront about that. A flag is a reason to look first, never the answer.
lines.note: Weight on 'never the answer'. Lowers and settles, candid rather than defensive.

lines.text: So the radiologist still reads the scan and makes the call. Every time Aidoc gets feedback, it makes a change.
lines.intent: human stays in the loop, then feedback
lines.note: Weight on 'makes the call'. Second sentence is a brisk, matter of fact turn.

lines.text: Next, the hospital plans phone alerts for stroke and pulmonary embolism teams, built for triage, not diagnosis. Clinicians would see the images on their phones and call in a response team right away.
lines.note: Weight on 'phones'. Slightly forward, then eases on 'right away'.

lines.text: The machine moves the line. A doctor still reads it.
lines.intent: closing line, lands lower and certain
lines.note: Two short statements. Weight on 'still reads it'. Lowest and most certain delivery of the film.
